title: Stabilization of a closed inverse system with finitely presented limit
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a nonempty directed set, and $(U_i,q_i,r_{ji})$ an inverse system of $S$-schemes, where $q_i:U_i\to S$ and $r_{ji}:U_j\to U_i$ for $j\ge i$ satisfy $q_i\circ r_{ji}=q_j$. Assume each $U_i$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], each $q_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and each transition $r_{ji}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $(U,(\rho_i))$ be its inverse limit in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], with induced morphism $q:U\to S$. If $q$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then there exists $i_0\in I$ such that every projection $\rho_i:U\to U_i$ for $i\ge i_0$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 081B, label lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed, clause (3), applied to the identity of the limit

proof.text: Fix $a\in I$. Cover $U_a$ by finitely many affine opens $V_{a,t}$ mapping into affine opens $W_t=\operatorname{Spec}R_t$ of $S$ such that $B_{a,t}=\Gamma(V_{a,t},\mathcal O)$ is finitely generated over $R_t$. Such a cover exists by local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: take an affine open cover of $S$, and for each member use the affine cover of its preimage provided by the definition. Together these charts cover $U_a$. Quasi-compactness of $U_a$ gives a finite subcover. For $i\ge a$ write $V_{i,t}=r_{ia}^{-1}(V_{a,t})$ and $V_t=\rho_a^{-1}(V_{a,t})$. The affine description of closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] shows that $V_{i,t}$ is affine and its ring $B_{i,t}$ is a quotient of $B_{a,t}$; all transitions of these rings are surjective.

For each $t$, the open-restriction and affine clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] give $V_t=\operatorname{Spec} B_t$ with $B_t=\varinjlim_{i\ge a} B_{i,t}$. The nonempty directed tail $I_{\ge a}$ is a small filtered category. Every colimit element comes from some stage by clause (1) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]; since $B_{a,t}\to B_{i,t}$ is surjective, $B_{a,t}\to B_t$ is surjective. Moreover $q(V_t)\subset W_t$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives that $B_t$ is finitely presented over $R_t$. This uses local finite presentation of the limit, with no quasi-separatedness assumption on the stages.

Choose an $R_t$-algebra surjection $P_t=R_t[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B_{a,t}$ using the finite generators of step 1. Its composite $P_t\twoheadrightarrow B_t$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg], its kernel is generated by finitely many polynomials $h_1,\ldots,h_m$. Their images $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ in $B_{a,t}$ generate $\ker(B_{a,t}\to B_t)$: lift any kernel element to $P_t$, where it belongs to $(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$, and take its image. Hence $B_t=B_{a,t}/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$.

Each $f_l$ has zero image in the colimit. Apply the eventual equality of representatives clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] to each $f_l$ and $0$, then use a finite directed upper bound, to obtain a common stage $b_t\ge a$ where every $f_l$ vanishes. At every $i\ge b_t$ we have $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\subset\ker(B_{a,t}\to B_{i,t})\subset\ker(B_{a,t}\to B_t)=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, so the kernels coincide. Since $B_{a,t}\to B_{i,t}$ is surjective, $B_{i,t}\to B_t$ is an isomorphism. For the empty generator list the same argument holds already at $a$.

Take a common upper bound $b$ of $a$ and the finitely many $b_t$. For $i\ge b$, each restriction $V_t\to V_{i,t}$ of $\rho_i$ is an isomorphism, as its ring map was shown to be an isomorphism. The opens $V_{i,t}$ cover $U_i$. Write $g_t:V_{i,t}\to V_t$ for the local inverses. For $H=V_{i,t}\cap V_{i,s}$, the identity $\rho_i\circ g_t=\mathrm{id}$ shows that $g_t|_H$ lands in $\rho_i^{-1}(H)=V_t\cap V_s$; the same holds for $g_s|_H$. The restriction of the isomorphism $V_t\to V_{i,t}$ identifies $V_t\cap V_s$ with $H$, and both restricted maps are its inverse, so they agree. No overlap is assumed affine. Glue these inverses by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to a global inverse $U_i\to U$. Both composites are identities because they are identities on this open cover and its inverse image cover. If the finite cover is empty, $U_a$ and every later $U_i$ and $U$ are empty, and their unique maps are isomorphisms. This proves the assertion for every $i\ge b$.
